column7: ChangePassword, ActivateMFA, and DisableMFA each spare the caller's own session from their post-change session purge by resolving keepSessionToken via storage.GetSession (`if s, serr := c.storage.GetSession(ctx, keepSessionToken); serr == nil { keepID = s.ID; keepHash = s.SessionToken }`). The `serr == nil` guard collapsed two different situations into one: keepSessionToken=="" ("no session to spare", keepID legitimately 0) and keepSessionToken!="" but GetSession failing (also keepID==0) -- both ended in the SAME full purge, including the caller's own session, with nothing distinguishing "the caller asked us not to spare a session" from "we could not tell which session to spare, so we killed them all". The widened purge is the correct fail-closed fallback (we cannot prove which session is the caller's, so revoking all of them is safer than guessing) and is NOT changed by this fix -- only its silence was. Worst case this masked: a storage hiccup on this one lookup during MFA activation could log the user out before the one-time recovery codes (returned in the response body, never stored in retrievable form) were ever displayed. Fixed by extracting resolution into resolveKeepSession (account.go), which now logs and writes EventKeepSessionLookupFailed when a supplied keepSessionToken fails to resolve, at all three call sites. The sibling finding -- deleteSessionsForUserAndEvict's own purge call failing outright (DeleteSessionsForUserExcept error), silently discarded by all 8 of its call sites -- is fixed at that function's own single choke point via the new EventSessionRevocationFailed, the returned-error analogue of the pre-existing EventSessionRevocationPanicked. Proving tests force each fault via a storage-wrapper stub: RED (audit-write lines removed) -- the lookup/purge failure still widens correctly but 0 audit rows are written; GREEN -- exactly 1 audit row per site, full purge unchanged. opScopedBestEffortTables (server/faultops) gained matching entries (GetSession on mfa/activate, mfa/disable, change-password; DeleteSessionsForUserExcept on mfa/disable, webauthn/register/finish), each gated on requireLogSubstring tied to the new log line -- a regression that silences the log would also silence the exemption, re-surfacing the oracle violation rather than being permanently waved through.
